findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 7897d79c0254549b845aec628079e38e09dee6e96c0723fe32201ca9553bba33; all 7 declared sources passed current access review.

Claims remain bounded to MRX document-control guidance, Texas conveyance and recording context, and IRS disposition and basis recordkeeping context. No source is converted into private title, document validity, contract meaning, recordability, offer terms, owner net, legal or tax treatment, payment, closing, or transaction advice.

The article invents no real owner, property, buyer, contract, transaction, price range, production, reserves, forecast, testimonial, success rate, or owner-specific legal, tax, accounting, title, appraisal, engineering, investment, or transaction conclusion.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Selling Mineral Rights: Selling Process For Mineral Owners (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX seller-control guide separates source documents from working records and treats proposals, agreements, deeds, payment, delivery, and recording as different transaction states.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to place a package-completeness index inside the broader owner-controlled process; it does not restate transaction stages or conclude title, document effect, offer quality, payment, closing, or whether to sell.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, The Hidden Traps in Selling Mineral Rights (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX hidden-traps guide says a possible sale package may refer to exhibits, schedules, incorporated terms, addenda, amendments, signature records, and other connected documents that should be obtained before substantive review.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to support tracing referenced components for completeness; it does not reproduce clause-trigger analysis or interpret any document, right, adjustment, deadline, obligation, remedy, or closing condition.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, How the Step-by-Step Process of Selling Texas Mineral Rights Works (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX Texas process guide distinguishes organizing records from certifying title and treats signing, payment, deed delivery, and recording as a controlled sequence of separate events.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to keep visible document copies and event records distinct in the index; it does not determine title, conveyance, delivery, payment, recording, tax treatment, or a transaction outcome.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Legislature, Property Code Chapter 5, Conveyances (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Chapter 5 contains Texas conveyance provisions, including statutory requirements addressed to the actual instrument and transaction circumstances.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to explain why a private package index cannot establish conveyance, delivery, authority, validity, legal effect, or ownership; no provision is applied to a particular owner or document.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Legislature, Property Code Chapter 12, Recording of Instruments (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: Texas Property Code Chapter 12 addresses recording instruments concerning property and states conditions under which an instrument may be recorded.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to distinguish an actual instrument and recording evidence from a private completeness index; it does not determine recordability, delivery, validity, priority, ownership, or legal effect.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 544, Sales and Other Dispositions of Assets (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Publication 544 explains that basis and adjusted basis are used in determining gain or loss from a sale or other disposition of property.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to explain why disposition and basis records may belong in a restricted professional workflow; it does not classify a mineral interest, determine basis, calculate gain or loss, choose tax treatment, or provide a retention rule.

sources_inspected.label: Internal Revenue Service, Publication 551, Basis of Assets (accessed 2026-08-14)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: IRS Publication 551 explains basis concepts and says accurate records should be kept for items that affect the basis of property.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses it only to support identifying the existence and restricted location of potential basis records; it does not determine which records apply, allocate basis, compute tax, choose reporting, or prescribe a retention period.
